title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
oneLinerQuestion: Find the minimum total cost to connect all 2D points into a single connected component.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Min Cost to Connect All Points problem requires finding the minimum total cost to make all points connected such that there is exactly one simple path between any two points without cycles, forming a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). The edge cost between any two coordinates (xi, yi) and (xj, yj) is defined by their Manhattan distance: |xi - xj| + |yi - yj|. Since every point can connect to every other point, this forms a complete dense graph with V vertices and O(V^2) edges. Prim's Algorithm grows the MST greedily starting from an arbitrary origin (such as index 0). In each iteration, it selects the cheapest available cross-edge connecting an already visited node in the tree to an unvisited node outside the tree. Using a Min-Heap (or an array-based min-distance lookup) allows us to iteratively incorporate all V vertices with minimal connection weight.

- Step 1: Base Case & State Allocation — Let `n = points.length`. If `n <= 1`, all points are already connected at zero cost; return `0`. Allocate a visited set or boolean array `visited = new Array(n).fill(false)` and an accumulator `totalCost = 0`.

- Step 2: Priority Queue / Min-Cost Initialization — Initialize a Min-Heap storing `[cost, nodeIndex]` pairs. Seed the priority queue with the arbitrary starting node 0 at cost 0: `minHeap.enqueue([0, 0])`. (Alternatively, initialize a `minDist` array with `minDist[0] = 0` and all other entries set to `Infinity` for an O(V^2) linear scan).

- Step 3: Prim's Greedy Expansion Loop — Execute a loop until all `n` vertices are included in the tree: maintain a counter `connected = 0`, looping `while (connected < n && minHeap.size() > 0)`.

- Step 4: Extract Minimum Weight Crossing Edge — Pop the minimum cost edge: `const [cost, u] = minHeap.dequeue()`. If `visited[u]` is already true, this node has already been integrated via a cheaper path; discard and continue.

- Step 5: Incorporate Vertex into MST — Mark `visited[u] = true`, accumulate the edge weight: `totalCost += cost`, and increment `connected++`.

- Step 6: Relaxation to Adjacent Unvisited Nodes — For every unvisited node `v` from `0` to `n - 1`: if `!visited[v]`, compute the Manhattan distance `dist = Math.abs(points[u][0] - points[v][0]) + Math.abs(points[u][1] - points[v][1])`. Push `[dist, v]` into the Min-Heap.

- Step 7: Termination & Result Return — Once `connected === n`, all points form a unified spanning tree with minimal total edge weight. Return `totalCost`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2 log N) using a standard binary heap across the O(N^2) total edges of the complete graph (or O(N^2) optimal time when maintaining an array of minimum distances to the current MST instead of a priority queue). Space Complexity: O(N^2) auxiliary space for storing candidate edges in the Min-Heap (or O(N) auxiliary space using the array-based Prim's algorithm).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION minCostConnectPoints(points):
    N = LENGTH(points), adj = HASH_MAP_OF_LISTS()
    FOR i FROM 0 TO N - 1 DO:
        FOR j FROM i + 1 TO N - 1 DO:
            dist = ABS(points[i][0] - points[j][0]) + ABS(points[i][1] - points[j][1])
            APPEND [dist, j] TO adj[i]; APPEND [dist, i] TO adj[j]
        END FOR
    END FOR
    res = 0, visit = SET(), minHeap = MinHeap([[0, 0]])
    WHILE LENGTH(visit) < N DO:
        [cost, i] = POP(minHeap)
        IF i IN visit THEN CONTINUE
        res = res + cost; ADD i TO visit
        FOR neiCost, nei IN adj[i] DO:
            IF nei NOT IN visit THEN PUSH [neiCost, nei] TO minHeap
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
